To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) a tangential dilation is an invertible generalization of the classical dilation; (2) it has a slope transform that is the discrete analog of the Fourier transform; and (3) this transform has the properties of the Legendre transform and the ¢ A transform.

the slope transform provides the analytical power which Fourier transforms lend to linear signal processing; and that the tangential dilation, which describes the touching between differentiable surfaces, is a morphological operator that generalizes dilation, but is still invertible.
the slope transform is a morphological Fourier transform, that it can be computed in O(n log n) steps using a fast algorithm, and that it is a powerful tool for morphological data processing.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of mathematical methods for describing and analysing shapes, and the development of tools for the analysis of shapes.
the development of the slope transform as a tool for the analysis of the morphological structure of signals.
the development of a theory of tangential morphology which is analogous to the Fourier theory of linear signal processing.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the slope transform is a generalization of the Fourier transform to the realm of tangential morphologies, which provides a powerful tool for morphological signal processing.
the slope transform is an important new tool for the analysis of data from a scanning probe microscope, in particular the scanning tunnelling and atomic force microscopes.
the slope transform is a powerful tool for morphological analysis of data, and that it is well suited for implementation on a computer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a mathematical theory for morphological signal processing.
we have developed a new mathematical tool for morphological data processing, which has a rich mathematical structure and a variety of applications.
the slope transform is to morphological signal processing what the Fourier transform is to linear signal processing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tangential morphological signal processing provides an analytical power which has not been previously recognized, and which can be used for morphological data interpretation.
the slope transform provides a natural framework for the morphological analysis of differentiable surfaces, and in particular for the morphological study of curvature.
the slope transform provides a powerful tool to analyze morphological signals, which is not limited to images.
